Era II

2016: the first large-scale push — and a surge of optimism.

The Digital Mammography DREAM Challenge was the first large-scale effort to build breast-cancer AI — and we took part. The hope was that a crowdsourced competition would simply solve it.

1,000+ participants · 126 teams · 44 countries
~640,000 mammograms

Best model AUC 0.858 → ensemble 0.895 → ensemble + a radiologist 0.942. The winner, Therapixel, spun out MammoScreen — still in clinical use today.

Schaffter et al., JAMA Network Open 2020;3(3):e200265.

Era II

2020: Google publishes its breast-cancer AI model.

McKinney et al., Nature 2020 (Google Health, UK + US) — a deep-learning system read screening mammograms stand-alone.

false positives −5.7% US / −1.2% UK
false negatives −9.4% US / −2.7% UK
AUC +11.5% vs avg radiologist
2nd-reader workload −88%

Results are promising — but again, only on retrospective, clean data.

Era II

Three commercial models, independently validated on 8,800 women.

Salim et al., JAMA Oncology 2020 tested three commercial algorithms on an external Stockholm cohort.

best (Algorithm 1) AUC 0.956
AI + first reader 88.6% sens @ 93% spec
exceeded two human readers

Three vendors, external data — the evidence is looking good.

Era II

Retrospective data isn't enough to drive adoption.

Enriched cases, lab conditions, no real workflow — CAD had good retrospective numbers too. The bar is prospective deployment, and real-world uptake has been slow.

Era II

2026: the averages look strong — so where do these models still fail?

Our DBT audit (EMBED, 163,449 exams): overall AUC 0.91 — but detection drops by histologic subtype.

Common ductal cancers are flagged ~86% of the time; rarer special subtypes — tubular, papillary, colloid — far less, 57–62% (small n).

Sensitivity also falls on dense breasts, in-situ, and calcifications (0.55–0.66) even as AUC stays ~0.80–0.88. And it doesn't transfer — specificity 31–54% on women with implants.

Trivedi group — DBT subgroup audit (Nat Commun 2026) · Du H et al. "Beyond Screening" 2026. Chart redrawn from the subtype figure.

Rare special subtypes are detected far less often (small n)
Era II → Era III

The detection score rises for years before the cancer is visible.

Hickman et al., Radiology 2026 — three detection systems across sequential screens (31,394 individuals). For future cancers the AI score is elevated up to 10 years before diagnosis; cancer-free individuals stay flat.

Combined predictive AUC 0.63–0.67 vs 0.57 for breast density.

Detection is blurring into risk. We stop asking the image about the lesion — and start asking it about the patient. That is Era III.
